fixes.explanation: That's right. If God says a wicked man will surely die and Ezekiel doesn't speak up, the man dies in his iniquity, “…yet I will hold you accountable for his blood.” (Ezekiel 33:8). God puts the weight of the job right on the watchman. That's a heavy part, and I think Ezekiel felt it.

Babylon is a fair guess, friend, but this verse doesn't name it. God says He has made Ezekiel a watchman “…for the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 33:7). That's his post. One watchman can't cover the whole map, and he isn't asked to.

Egypt doesn't come up here, friend. God says He has made Ezekiel a watchman “…for the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 33:7). A watchman with the wrong post would be staring at the wrong horizon all day. This one's post has a name on it.

Too slow is a fair guess, friend, but nobody's tapping a watch here. Verse 17 says, “Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’…” (Ezekiel 33:17). Their charge isn't about speed. They're saying the way itself isn't just, and that's a much bigger thing to say.

Too strict is a fair guess, friend, but that's not what they say. Verse 17 says, “Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’…” (Ezekiel 33:17). Strict would be a gripe about the rules. They go further and say it isn't just at all. That's quite a claim right after God said He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked (Ezekiel 33:11).

Family is a natural guess, friend, but it isn't the word here. God says, “But I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.” (Ezekiel 33:20). The word is ways, and it's said to each of you. No group discount, no group blame. Each person's own walk is what counts.
